title: Negative repository search is not exhaustive absence evidence

observed: Authenticated repository code search for the literal identifier M-004 returned zero results during this run.
The default-branch file operations/continuity/records/CM-1019-identifier-materialization-boundary.json was fetched directly and contains multiple literal M-004 occurrences.
The active queue requires exhaustive branch inventory or equivalent history traversal before M-004, M-005, or M-006 may be classified as unlocated.
inferred: A zero-result repository code-search response is coverage-ambiguous and cannot establish that an identifier is absent from the default branch, other refs, or reachable history.
Search-index availability, indexing lag, query semantics, or connector coverage may produce false-negative absence signals.
proposed: Represent every negative search result with coverage_status=absence_unproven unless accompanied by a retained coverage manifest that names all traversed refs, reachable commits, object classes, and tool limits.
Require direct immutable-object inspection for any candidate used to resolve or reject an identifier origin.
superseded: Treating zero code-search matches as proof that a repository object does not exist.
Promoting search-index absence to identifier origin_status=unlocated without exhaustive traversal evidence.
unresolved: Whether the zero-result response was caused by indexing state, connector query semantics, repository visibility, or another coverage limitation.
The exhaustive ref and reachable-commit traversal required for final origin classification remains incomplete.
The origin_event for M-004, M-005, and M-006 remains unresolved.

decision_rule: Negative search evidence may identify a traversal lead or tool limitation, but it cannot prove repository absence or support origin_status=unlocated unless a retained exhaustive coverage manifest demonstrates every accepted search domain was traversed without unresolved limits.
falsification_routes: Demonstrate that the code-search response did return the directly fetched M-004-containing object during the same run and query scope.
Produce a documented search contract proving zero results exhaustively cover all refs, reachable commits, and relevant object classes.
Complete exhaustive traversal and retain a manifest that independently supports an unlocated classification.
